skill.name: writing-shape
skill.description: Guides a conversational process that turns a markdown source file of notes or fragments into a separate article draft.
skill.summary: Turns raw markdown notes into a structured article through guided drafting.
skill.author: mattpocock

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 49 contains Markdown inline code examples for callout syntax, not Ruby or shell command execution. There is no executable script or runtime context in this skill file.
Line 12 asks for an article save path and says to re-read that article file to preserve user edits. It does not request system enumeration, hidden file discovery, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Raw notes often lack a clear argument and order. This skill guides a conversational drafting loop that turns markdown material into a publishable article.
actual_capabilities: Reads a markdown source file fully before drafting begins.
Drafts two or three candidate openings with different article angles.
Builds the article paragraph by paragraph with user review.
Discusses format choices for prose, lists, tables, callouts, quotes, and code blocks.
Appends agreed blocks to a separate article file during the session.
Identifies missing source material and asks the user to supply it or cut the section.
limitations: Requires a user-provided markdown source file or equivalent raw material.
Does not edit the original raw material file.
Does not publish the article or format it for a specific platform.
Does not invent missing examples, claims, or evidence.

use_cases.title: Turn Notes Into a Blog Draft
use_cases.description: Shape scattered markdown notes into an article with a clear opening, sequence, and conclusion.

use_cases.title: Develop Teaching Material
use_cases.description: Convert lesson fragments into a structured article that explains concepts in the right order.

use_cases.title: Refine Internal Thought Pieces
use_cases.description: Work through rough ideas with direct editorial questions before sharing a polished draft.

prompt_templates.title: Start From Raw Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a basic article shaping session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-shape on my source notes and create a separate article draft. Show two or three opening options before writing more.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Strong Angle
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for comparing possible article theses.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read my markdown notes and propose three openings with different arguments. Explain what each opening commits the article to prove.

prompt_templates.title: Build Section by Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for controlled drafting with user approval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Shape this material into an article one section at a time. Ask before each new beat and write only the agreed block.

prompt_templates.title: Pressure Test the Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for rigorous editorial review during drafting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-shape as a strict editor. Challenge weak transitions, test every paragraph against the opening, and name gaps before drafting.

output_examples.input: A markdown file with scattered conference notes, partial arguments, and a few strong quotes.
output_examples.output: The assistant offers three possible openings, helps choose one, then drafts the article paragraph by paragraph.

output_examples.input: A rough technical draft with repeated ideas and unclear section order.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies what each paragraph must do, cuts weak repeats, and rebuilds the article flow.

output_examples.input: A transcript with useful anecdotes but no written structure.
output_examples.output: The assistant extracts usable fragments, asks for missing examples, and shapes them into a coherent article.

best_practices: Provide the source material and desired article file path at the start.
Choose an opening before drafting the rest of the article.
Review each paragraph as it is added so the draft stays aligned.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to edit the raw source file directly.
Do not expect it to invent facts that are missing from the source material.
Do not skip the opening choice, because it defines the article argument.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It works best with a markdown file containing notes, fragments, a transcript, or a rough draft.

faq.question: Will it change my original notes?
faq.answer: No. The skill treats the source material as read-only and writes to a separate article file.

faq.question: Does it write the full article at once?
faq.answer: No. It builds the article paragraph by paragraph after the user agrees on each direction.

faq.question: Can it help choose the article angle?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts by drafting candidate openings that imply different arguments or structures.

faq.question: Can it add examples that are not in my notes?
faq.answer: It should not invent examples. It names the gap and asks you to supply material or cut the section.
